Kelvin finds the order one position at a time, and in the worst case every wrong guess is tried before the right one.

**Wrong guesses.** Suppose Kelvin already knows the first k−1 pads. Then 10−k+1 candidates remain for position k, so in the worst case there are 10−k wrong guesses. Each wrong guess costs k hops: k−1 hops to retrace the known pads, plus 1 hop onto the wrong pad. Once only one candidate remains, no guess is needed.

Total hops spent on wrong guesses:

$$\sum_{k=1}^{10} k(10-k) = 10\cdot 55 - 385 = 165.$$

**Final run.** With the whole order known, Kelvin makes one complete crossing: 10 hops over the pads plus 1 hop to the far bank, which is 11 hops.

**Total.** 165 + 11 = 176.

ANSWER: 176
